+## Project
+
+`musicrs` is a Rust library port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC): the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification, R. O. Schmidt) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone arrays. Library crate only (no binary), Rust edition 2024.
+
+## Commands
+
+```sh
+cargo build
+cargo test                                   # unit tests, doctests, integration test
+cargo test --lib                             # unit tests in src/ only
+cargo test --test integration_test           # WAV-based DOA accuracy test
+cargo test estimate_doa_from_rank1_covariance # single test by name filter
+cargo test --test integration_test -- --nocapture  # see the pass summary println
+cargo clippy --all-targets
+cargo fmt
+```
+
+The integration test reads `./tests/data/single-source` with a relative path, so run it from the repo root (cargo does this by default).
+
+## Architecture
+
+Two modules, re-exported from `src/lib.rs` (`MusicEstimator`, `analytic_signal`, `stft`):
+
+- `src/stft.rs` — signal preprocessing with `rustfft`. `analytic_signal` (FFT-based Hilbert transform, turns a real channel into a complex one) and `stft` (returns `[freq_bin][window]`, `nfft/2 + 1` bins, no windowing function).
+- `src/music.rs` — `MusicEstimator` (antenna `[x, y]` positions in metres, angle grid size, search interval in radians, sample rate). Defaults: Kinect 4-mic linear array, 720 steps over [0, 2π), 16 kHz.

+  - `ifb_music_spectrum` is the wideband variant: per-mic STFT, per-bin cross-spectral matrix averaged over windows, narrowband spectra combined by geometric mean.
+  - Linear algebra is split across crates: `nalgebra` (`DMatrix<Complex<f64>>`) is the public/working type; `faer` is used only inside `hermitian_eigen` for the Hermitian eigendecomposition (conversion in and out, results re-sorted ascending since faer does not guarantee order). No LAPACK dependency.
+

+
+`steering_vector` is tuned to match the analytic-signal phase convention of the test data: positive exponent below Nyquist, negative above Nyquist (aliased bins), and a real `cos(phase)` vector when the frequency is within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist. Changing the eigenvector conjugation in `hermitian_eigen` or these signs breaks the integration test.
+## Tests and data

+- `tests/integration_test.rs` runs `estimate_doa` (n_sources = 1, after `analytic_signal` per channel) on every WAV in `tests/data/single-source/` and requires ±5° accuracy. Filenames encode ground truth: `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`. Files are 4-channel, 24-bit PCM, 16 kHz, read with `hound`.
+- Because the array is linear along x, θ and 360°−θ are indistinguishable; at Nyquist, 180°±θ are also accepted. The test accounts for this; keep it in mind when interpreting estimates.
+- `tests/data/single-source/README.md` still describes the data as numpy arrays; the files are now WAV (see commit "replace npy files with wav").
+- Unit tests live in `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside each source file and use `approx`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

`musicrs` is a Rust library port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC): the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification, R. O. Schmidt) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone arrays. Library crate only (no binary), Rust edition 2024.

## Commands

```sh
cargo build
cargo test                                   # unit tests, doctests, integration test
cargo test --lib                             # unit tests in src/ only
cargo test --test integration_test           # WAV-based DOA accuracy test
cargo test estimate_doa_from_rank1_covariance # single test by name filter
cargo test --test integration_test -- --nocapture  # see the pass summary println
cargo clippy --all-targets
cargo fmt
```

The integration test reads `./tests/data/single-source` with a relative path, so run it from the repo root (cargo does this by default).

## Architecture

Two modules, re-exported from `src/lib.rs` (`MusicEstimator`, `analytic_signal`, `stft`):

- `src/stft.rs` — signal preprocessing with `rustfft`. `analytic_signal` (FFT-based Hilbert transform, turns a real channel into a complex one) and `stft` (returns `[freq_bin][window]`, `nfft/2 + 1` bins, no windowing function).
- `src/music.rs` — `MusicEstimator` (antenna `[x, y]` positions in metres, angle grid size, search interval in radians, sample rate). Defaults: Kinect 4-mic linear array, 720 steps over [0, 2π), 16 kHz.
  - Pipeline in `estimate_doa`: covariance `X·Xᴴ/N` → `noise_subspace` (eigenvectors of the smallest `n − n_sources` eigenvalues) → `spectrum` (`1/‖Eₙᴴ a(θ)‖²` over the grid) → `find_peaks` (circular local maxima, highest first). Angles are radians.
  - `ifb_music_spectrum` is the wideband variant: per-mic STFT, per-bin cross-spectral matrix averaged over windows, narrowband spectra combined by geometric mean.
  - Linear algebra is split across crates: `nalgebra` (`DMatrix<Complex<f64>>`) is the public/working type; `faer` is used only inside `hermitian_eigen` for the Hermitian eigendecomposition (conversion in and out, results re-sorted ascending since faer does not guarantee order). No LAPACK dependency.

### Sign conventions (fragile, test-driven)

`steering_vector` is tuned to match the analytic-signal phase convention of the test data: positive exponent below Nyquist, negative above Nyquist (aliased bins), and a real `cos(phase)` vector when the frequency is within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist. Changing the eigenvector conjugation in `hermitian_eigen` or these signs breaks the integration test.
## Tests and data

- `tests/integration_test.rs` runs `estimate_doa` (n_sources = 1, after `analytic_signal` per channel) on every WAV in `tests/data/single-source/` and requires ±5° accuracy. Filenames encode ground truth: `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`. Files are 4-channel, 24-bit PCM, 16 kHz, read with `hound`.
- Because the array is linear along x, θ and 360°−θ are indistinguishable; at Nyquist, 180°±θ are also accepted. The test accounts for this; keep it in mind when interpreting estimates.
- `tests/data/single-source/README.md` still describes the data as numpy arrays; the files are now WAV (see commit "replace npy files with wav").
- Unit tests live in `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside each source file and use `approx`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project

`musicrs` is a Rust library port of [pyMUSIC](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/pyMUSIC): the MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification, R. O. Schmidt) algorithm for Direction-of-Arrival (DOA) estimation with microphone arrays. Library crate only (no binary), Rust edition 2024.

## Commands

```sh
cargo build
cargo test                                   # unit tests, doctests, integration test
cargo test --lib                             # unit tests in src/ only
cargo test --test integration_test           # WAV-based DOA accuracy test
cargo test estimate_doa_from_rank1_covariance # single test by name filter
cargo test --test integration_test -- --nocapture  # see the pass summary println
cargo clippy --all-targets
cargo fmt
```

The integration test reads `./tests/data/single-source` with a relative path, so run it from the repo root (cargo does this by default).

## Architecture

Two modules, re-exported from `src/lib.rs` (`MusicEstimator`, `analytic_signal`, `stft`):

- `src/stft.rs` — signal preprocessing with `rustfft`. `analytic_signal` (FFT-based Hilbert transform, turns a real channel into a complex one) and `stft` (returns `[freq_bin][window]`, `nfft/2 + 1` bins, no windowing function).
- `src/music.rs` — `MusicEstimator` (antenna `[x, y]` positions in metres, angle grid size, search interval in radians, sample rate). Defaults: Kinect 4-mic linear array, 720 steps over [0, 2π), 16 kHz.
  - Pipeline in `estimate_doa`: covariance `X·Xᴴ/N` → `noise_subspace` (eigenvectors of the smallest `n − n_sources` eigenvalues) → `spectrum` (`1/‖Eₙᴴ a(θ)‖²` over the grid) → `find_peaks` (circular local maxima, highest first). Angles are radians.
  - `ifb_music_spectrum` is the wideband variant: per-mic STFT, per-bin cross-spectral matrix averaged over windows, narrowband spectra combined by geometric mean.
  - Linear algebra is split across crates: `nalgebra` (`DMatrix<Complex<f64>>`) is the public/working type; `faer` is used only inside `hermitian_eigen` for the Hermitian eigendecomposition (conversion in and out, results re-sorted ascending since faer does not guarantee order). No LAPACK dependency.

### Sign conventions (fragile, test-driven)

`steering_vector` is tuned to match the analytic-signal phase convention of the test data: positive exponent below Nyquist, negative above Nyquist (aliased bins), and a real `cos(phase)` vector when the frequency is within 0.5 Hz of Nyquist. Changing the eigenvector conjugation in `hermitian_eigen` or these signs breaks the integration test.
## Tests and data

- `tests/integration_test.rs` runs `estimate_doa` (n_sources = 1, after `analytic_signal` per channel) on every WAV in `tests/data/single-source/` and requires ±5° accuracy. Filenames encode ground truth: `single-source_<freq>Hz_<doa>deg_<duration>s.wav`. Files are 4-channel, 24-bit PCM, 16 kHz, read with `hound`.
- Because the array is linear along x, θ and 360°−θ are indistinguishable; at Nyquist, 180°±θ are also accepted. The test accounts for this; keep it in mind when interpreting estimates.
- `tests/data/single-source/README.md` still describes the data as numpy arrays; the files are now WAV (see commit "replace npy files with wav").
- Unit tests live in `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside each source file and use `approx`.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.
